tier_reason: First-party bar charts in doc/Bolt Performance.md (images under doc/_images) compare Bolt with Lua 5.4 on a named CPU (Ryzen 9 3900X) and Bolt's MSVC flags are public in bolt/CMakeLists.txt, but the Lua 5.4 minor version and build are unstated ('recommended build instructions, or a provided pre-compiled binary') and the foreign-language benchmark sources the doc points to (benchmarks/_foreign) are not in the repository, so it falls short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Versus Lua 5.4 (chart values, ms, lower is better): fib(30) 52 vs 62; closure iterator (10M iterations) 188 vs 300; Mandelbrot 87 vs 184; Vec2 create-create-add 39 (14 with mimalloc) vs 85; Vec2 add 12.7 (4.7 with mimalloc) vs 26.0; Vec2 distance 31 vs 96; binary_tree(4,12) 274 vs 339; spectral(500) 376 vs 471; nbody(500000) 744 vs 1097. Slower on fannkuch(9): 281 vs 148. Ratios derived from page data: about 1.2x (fib) to 3.1x (Vec2 distance) with the system allocator, and 5.5x to 6.1x on the two Vec2 allocation benchmarks with mimalloc.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Bolt: MSVC (version not stated) using the repo's CMake configuration; bolt/CMakeLists.txt sets /O2 /Ob2 /Oi /Ot /Oy /GL /GS- /GR- /arch:AVX for Release (and -Ofast -O3 for non-MSVC builds). Baselines: 'built to recommended build instructions, or using a provided pre-compiled binary, depending on which is faster'; no flags or versions beyond the major version given.
corrections.caveats: First-party benchmark; the numbers are bar-chart images in the doc (read from the PNGs), averages of 10 or 15 runs with no pinning or variance stated. The doc says the other languages' implementations are in benchmarks/_foreign, but that directory does not exist in the repository (404), so only the Bolt side of the benchmark code is public. Bolt is slower than Lua 5.4 on fannkuch(9) (281 vs 148 ms). Luau beats Bolt on binary_tree, nbody and fannkuch, Wren beats Bolt on binary_tree (247 vs 274 ms), and with the system allocator Luau and LuaJIT -joff beat Bolt on both Vec2 allocation benchmarks (Bolt only leads there with mimalloc). Only interpreters are compared (JIT runtimes excluded except LuaJIT -joff). The Lua 5.4 minor version and build flags are not stated, and Bolt was built on Windows with MSVC; the chart date is not given, so the numbers may predate the current code. Bolt is a statically typed language of its own, not a Lua drop-in.

notes: All chart values in the record match the PNGs exactly; license MIT, 816 stars, last commit 2026-01-05, not a fork. Shortcomings to record: baseline benchmark sources (benchmarks/_foreign) missing from repo, Lua 5.4 build unstated, slower than Lua 5.4 on fannkuch, needs mimalloc to lead on allocation-heavy benchmarks.

tier_reason: PR #8 reports a first-party CI comparison against upstream quickjs-ng master; the workflow (.github/workflows/bench-upstream.yml, bench/runtime.js, upstream tests/microbench.js, Octane pinned to a commit) is public, but it runs on a GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner with no CPU model and no named compiler, so it falls short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: PR #8 (fork 4679cbc vs upstream quickjs-ng 19dbe85, medians of 3 alternating runs): Octane 2.0 total score 2022 to 2385 (+18%; Gameboy -5%); upstream tests/microbench.js 1.18x faster (geomean); bench/runtime.js 1.57x faster with instructions down 35%; peak memory over full Octane +18% and qjs code size +12%. PR #9 (against the fork's own previous head, next ef7671b): Octane geomean 2324 to 2838 (+22.1%), DeltaBlue -2.8%. PR #12 (against next c861d16): time 19 faster, 0 slower, 20 unchanged (threshold 5%), geomean -21.2%; instructions 22 fewer, 0 more, 17 unchanged, geomean -20.9%; Octane same work in 2.4% fewer instructions.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: make BUILD_TYPE=Release for both fork and upstream on the same toolchain (CMake Release defaults); compiler not named.
corrections.hardware: GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runner (Linux/X64); CPU model not stated
corrections.caveats: Numbers come from PR descriptions and the fork's own CI workflow, not an independent run, and the runner CPU is unknown (shared cloud VMs). Only PR #8 compares against upstream quickjs-ng; PRs #9 and #12 measure against the fork's own earlier heads, so their gains are not additive with PR #8 against upstream without a fresh upstream run. PR #8 also reports costs: peak memory +18% over full Octane (CodeLoad 60 to 84 MB, PdfJS 18 to 23 MB), qjs code size +12%, Gameboy -5%, and regressions on microbench global_write (+50%) and array_for (+16%). The fork is days to weeks old (13 PRs, 2026-09-14 to 2026-09-29), has no stars, and its branches and commits are authored by an AI assistant (claude/... branches); bytecode version was bumped (BC_VERSION 35), so bytecode is not compatible with upstream. PR #12 states test262 shows 14 errors out of 82220, the same 14 as upstream's list, and Debug plus ASan/UBSan builds were clean. The baseline is upstream quickjs-ng, not Bellard's QuickJS. No indication the changes were proposed upstream.

notes: PR #8 numbers match; the record misreported PR #12 (it is 19 faster / 0 slower / 20 unchanged in time out of 39 benchmarks, geomean -21.2%; 22 is the instruction-count tally) and omitted PR #8's memory +18% and binary +12% costs, corrected above. Shortcomings: first-party CI only, CPU unknown, new 0-star AI-written fork, higher memory and code size than upstream.

tier_reason: The README compares with QuickJS only qualitatively ('The speed is comparable to QuickJS') and gives absolute footprint figures (10 kB RAM, about 100 kB ARM Thumb-2 ROM) with no QuickJS figure, so there is no measured advantage over the baseline.

corrections.caveats: No numbers for QuickJS are given, so the memory advantage is not quantified, and speed is stated to be merely comparable (not faster). MQuickJS supports only a subset of JavaScript close to ES5 (stricter mode), so it is not a drop-in QuickJS replacement. Kept as a notable tier D entry for the memory-footprint claim; the benchmark inputs (QuickJS microbench via 'make microbench', patched Octane) come from a separate tarball on bellard.org that is blocked here and was not opened.

notes: README text matches the record exactly; MIT, 6.2k stars, last commit 2026-09-26, not a fork. Not rejected: notable (6.2k stars) and the claim is footprint rather than speed. Shortcomings: no QuickJS numbers for memory, speed only 'comparable', ES5 subset. One WebSearch found no independent MQuickJS-vs-QuickJS numbers (only a Zig port's self-comparison).
